body:
[aida:reviewer] AUDIT DONE, RESULT IS CLEAN — and it turned up two substrate observations
I am sending rather than filing, per the operator's instruction.

WHY I RAN IT. BUG-1526 reddened eleven PRs for reasons unrelated to their code. The risk
that creates is a WRONGFUL REFUSAL: a verdict whose blocking reason was a red Build that
was actually the masked gate. Now that the gate is fixed, that is checkable, so I checked
it rather than assume it did not happen.

METHOD: every PR-*.json refusal in .aida/review-verdicts, scanned for a summary or finding
leaning on a build/CI failure as evidence. Five hits, each read in full.

    PR-1952   portability ratchet, step 28, naming protocol_cmd.rs:169-170
    PR-1972   three findings, all file:line; CI clause incidental
    PR-1987   three of four acceptance criteria failed against the RUNNING binary
    PR-1998   mine; rests on inspection, states so explicitly
    PR-2009   F1 is "the required check NEVER RAN" — absence, not a masked failure

NOT ONE OF THEM RESTS ON A MASKED STEP-12 RED. PR-1952 is the load-bearing case and it
settles the class: the portability ratchet is step 28, and BUG-1526 aborts at step 12, so
a PR that failed at 28 necessarily PASSED 12. Its red was real. PR-2009 is the inverse and
also clean — it refused because no Build existed at all, and separately filed BUG-1481 for
the false green that let it look mergeable.

So the masking cost us diagnosability, not correctness. No refusal needs revisiting.

TWO THINGS THE SWEEP EXPOSED.

1. PROVENANCE, measured by era rather than quoted as one number, because one number would
mislead:

       PR <1000      111 records    0 with reviewed_sha    (0%)
       PR 1000-1899  249 records    3                      (1%)
       PR >=1900     146 records   46                      (31%)

   506 records, 457 without a reviewed sha. The headline "90% lack provenance" is true and
   useless — the practice clearly started recently. The real number is that even in the
   current era it is 31%, so roughly two in three verdicts recorded TONIGHT-era cannot say
   which commit they examined. A verdict without a sha cannot be checked for staleness,
   which is the whole mechanism that makes `queue done` refuse.

2. THE VERDICT FILE IS SINGLE-SLOT AND PEOPLE ARE WORKING AROUND IT BY FILENAME. There are
   27 sidecar records — PR-1913-advisor.json, -r2, -r3, plus PR-1904/1916/1921/1924/1943/
   1945/1946/1948/1949/1952/1956/1957/1958/1959/1960/1964/1965/1970/1972/1973/1977/1979/
   2006/2014-advisor.json. `aida review record` overwrites PR-N.json, so a second reviewer
   or a second round destroys the first's findings, and the workaround is a name the tool
   does not read. PR-2009's own F3 says this out loud: "Recording this explicitly because a
   verdict file is overwritten". That is a reviewer defending against the substrate by
   hand.

   The consequence is not cosmetic. The orchestrator's phase-3 handshake reads PR-N.json.
   Every one of those 27 sidecars is invisible to it.

BOTH ARE YOURS TO DISPOSE OF. I am not filing them, and I am not claiming either is urgent
— nine PRs becoming diagnosable is worth more tonight than either. But the second one in
particular is a gap I would not want rediscovered by someone losing a verdict.

Nothing outstanding on my side. Reviewer queue is five specs, all with current-head
verdicts pending implementer rework, and #1978 is frozen and parked.
subject: Audit: NO refusal rests on masked step-12 CI — masking cost diagnosability, not correctness. Two substrate gaps found: verdict provenance (31% even now) and PR-N.json is single-slot (27 filename workarounds)
